html:
The Surinamese Interior War was fought from 1986 to 1992 between the army of Dési Bouterse and the Jungle Commando, a guerrilla force of Maroons led by Ronnie Brunswijk, his former bodyguard.

The war centred on the east of Suriname, near the border river with French Guiana. In November 1986 soldiers killed dozens of villagers, mostly women and children, at the Ndyuka village of Moiwana. Thousands of Maroons fled across the river to French Guiana as refugees.

A peace accord was signed in 1992. The war left the interior poor and armed, and Brunswijk later became a politician and vice-president. The Inter-American Court ruled against Suriname over the Moiwana massacre in 2005. The war was part of the long conflict over the land of the Maroon peoples and the rule of Bouterse.
sum: The Surinamese Interior War was fought from 1986 to 1992 between the army of Dési Bouterse and the Jungle Commando, a guerrilla force of Maroons led by Ronnie Brunswijk, his former bodyguard.
